messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High error rate detected on runtime shard us-east-1b for model redwood-r1. 5xx spike -> 320 errors/min over 5m. Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/completions. Paging on-call: @oncall-runtime-primary @oncall-infra-secondary. Incident dashboard: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-4721

Maria Chen: ack, I'm runtime primary, jumping in. Looking at pod logs now. Can support confirm customer facing scope?

Support Oncall: seeing multiple customer threads reporting timeouts and 500s, ~7 customers directly impacted (chat + embeddings). Triage note: some requests are being retried by clients causing increased load.

Jon Patel: I'm infra-secondary, available to help with networking / autoscaler. Maria, can you paste a couple of representative error traces?

Maria Chen: quick grep & tail from one node:
```
2026-03-14T16:02:41Z ERROR runtime::handler - kv cache miss; batch exec failed: CUDA out of memory
...
2026-03-14T16:02:43Z WARN  runtime::scheduler - worker 5 slow, queue depth 87
```
Seems like OOMs on a subset of GPUs after a large burst. Possibly batching suddenly increased due to retries.

Ashok Rao: If it's OOM we should consider temporarily lowering batch size and pinning model to quantized variant. I can push a temporary config to the serving group. Any objections?

Linda Park: I'm support lead for affected accounts, coordinating customer comms. If we enable a degraded-but-stable routing to redwood-r1-quant it may reduce quality but restore service quickly. Need decision on SLA comms.

Kevin Ortiz: Security Oncall here. Any signs of suspicious traffic patterns or malformed payloads? If it's retries from legit clients, prob not security. Support logs don't show unusual auth failures.

Maria Chen: I ran quick samples against the request patterns — no suspicious headers. Looks like retry storms from a batch of internal prod clients (analytics ingest). Not a credential issue.

Jon Patel: For mitigation I recommend: 1) throttle incoming rate via edge rules for the specific route, 2) push batch_size=8 for runtime group for 20m, 3) enable fallback routing to r1-quant for requests that exceed latency threshold. I'll own the edge throttle change.

Maria Chen: On it to push batch_size change. Ashok, can you prepare r1-quant slot and warm it? Need warm cache before rerouting.

Ashok Rao: Warming r1-quant now, ETA ~4m. I'll report when KV caches warmed.

Support Oncall: I'll update the customer-facing incident note: status -> "degraded, mitigation in progress". Asking product to confirm wording.

Incident Bot: Runbook pointer: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/runtime/oom-spike. Suggested playbook: reduce batching -> enable fallback model -> throttle at edge -> monitor errors to <50/min.

Maria Chen: Quick handoff note: I'm primary until 17:00 UTC then Jon takes over. If mitigation not stable by then, we'll extend the shift or call secondary in.

Linda Park: There's a coverage gap 17:00-18:00 UTC where product leads are in weekly sync. Recommend we schedule an on-call overlap for 30m. @Jon Patel can you cover an extra 30m if needed?

Jon Patel: I can extend 30m if needed. I'll also coordinate with infra-secondary to ensure autoscaler thresholds aren't causing churn.

Kevin Ortiz: Confirmed no security escalation. If we later find exfil attempts or anomalous auth, I'll join immediately. For now, route to runtime/infra.

Maria Chen: mitigation pushed: batch_size=8 on affected nodes, enabled soft-fallback route to r1-quant for requests >1.2s latency. Monitoring graphs... error rate dropping to 120/min and falling.

Support Oncall: Updated incident post. Notifying top 7 customers with ETA 30m.

Ashok Rao: r1-quant warmed, KV cache hit ratio ~0.6. Switching a small canary of traffic now.

Maria Chen: Can everyone acknowledge change and add to handoff notes? I'll summarize final state before I hand off at 17:00 UTC.

Jon Patel: ack. I'll keep the edge throttle rule sticky for 20m then reassess.

Incident Bot: Note: on-call handoff scheduled: Maria Chen -> Jon Patel at 17:00 UTC. Use /handoff confirm to record.

Maria Chen: final summary for handoff: root cause likely retry storm from analytic clients leading to increased batching -> OOM cascade on subset of GPUs. Short-term mitigations applied: throttle at edge, batch_size reduced, canary fallback to r1-quant. Error rate down ~75%. No security indicators. Support notified. Next steps: monitor 30m, plan for autoscaler tuning and durable fallback for model variants.

Jon Patel: thanks, good notes. I'll take over and coordinate autoscaler tuning if error rate creeps back up.

Security Oncall: acknowledged. If anything changes with auth or traffic profile, ping me immediately.

Support Oncall: ack, continuing customer comms.
